slot.brief: A mixed series–parallel capacitor network connected to batteries; find the equivalent capacitance and charge on a specified capacitor.

stem: Two $6$ V batteries are connected in series aiding across the capacitor network shown. Find the network's equivalent capacitance and the charge on $C_2$.

verdicts.working: The 2 μF and 4 μF capacitors are in parallel, giving 6 μF. In series with C₁ = 6 μF, the equivalent is 3 μF. The batteries provide 12 V, so the series charge is 36 μC; the parallel pair has 6 V across it, giving Q₂ = (2 μF)(6 V) = 12 μC.

working:
$C_{23}=2+4=6\ \mu\text{F}$
$C_{\text{eq}}=\dfrac{6\times6}{6+6}=3\ \mu\text{F}$
$V_{AB}=6+6=12\ \text{V}$
$Q_{\text{series}}=C_{\text{eq}}V_{AB}=36\ \mu\text{C}$
$V_{23}=\dfrac{Q_{\text{series}}}{C_{23}}=6\ \text{V}$
$Q_2=C_2V_{23}=12\ \mu\text{C}$

Independent check: The 2 μF and 4 μF capacitors are in parallel, giving 6 μF. In series with C₁ = 6 μF, the equivalent is 3 μF. The batteries provide 12 V, so the series charge is 36 μC; the parallel pair has 6 V across it, giving Q₂ = (2 μF)(6 V) = 12 μC.
solution: $C_2$ and $C_3$ are in parallel, so $C_{23}=2+4=6\ \mu\text{F}$. In series with $C_1=6\ \mu\text{F}$, $$C_{\text{eq}}=\frac{6\times6}{6+6}=3\ \mu\text{F}.$$ The batteries provide $12\ \text{V}$, so the series charge is $Q=3(12)=36\ \mu\text{C}$; hence $V_{23}=36/6=6\ \text{V}$ and $Q_2=2(6)=12\ \mu\text{C}$.

draft.stem: Two $6$ V batteries are connected in series aiding across the capacitor network shown. Find the network's equivalent capacitance and the charge on $C_2$.

figure.description: Draw two common terminals A and B, with A marked positive and B negative for the supply. Between A and B draw the capacitor network: from A, a capacitor labelled C1 = 6 μF leads in series to a junction X; connect X to B with two parallel branches, one containing C2 = 2 μF and the other C3 = 4 μF. Draw a separate branch directly between A and B containing two ideal 6 V battery symbols in series aiding; label each battery 6 V and mark the overall polarity + at A and − at B. Clearly show the junctions and capacitor connections.

draft.distractor_notes:
B: Treats all three capacitors as parallel across the full supply.
C: Finds the equivalent capacitance correctly but places the full supply voltage across $C_2$.
D: Treats the series combination of equal capacitances as having the same capacitance as either one.
